paragraphs: In Rhondda Cynon Taf the council's fostering service is Foster Wales Rhondda Cynon Taf, part of the national network of all 22 Welsh council fostering services. Children in care live with its carers or with independent agencies such as the services shown above. In February 2025 the council said 368 children were in foster care in the county and that it needed 163 more foster homes; across Wales it put the number of children in care at more than 7,000, against about 3,800 foster families.
Fostering in the county can mean anything from an overnight stay or a short break to a home for the longer term. Foster Wales RCT says it has more than 230 foster carers.

Its support page sets out how council carers are paid: a weekly child's allowance of £204 to £255 depending on the child's age, a carer's fee of £212.50 a week, and a retention payment of £1,000 a year paid in two instalments of £500. The skills fee can continue for up to three months between children, and the whole household gets a leisure pass. The service gives an example range of current carers' yearly income of £15,522 to £41,600, depending on how many children they look after, their ages and how long the carer has fostered.

In March 2026 The Fostering Network gave the RCT Pioneers, a group of the county's experienced carers, its group award at its annual wellbeing conference. Foster Wales RCT holds regular information sessions, in person at venues such as Pontypridd Library and Llantrisant Leisure Centre, and online.
Ask Foster Wales RCT and two or three of the services listed here what they pay, how they train new carers and how they support them, and compare the answers before you apply.
